title: A seismicity-rate alarm from the public JMA catalog came before 6 of 61 Japanese eruption onsets in 1999-2024 with an uncertain gain, and about 99% of its alarms had no eruption
abstract: We tested if shallow earthquake rates in the public JMA unified hypocenter catalog increase before Japanese eruption onsets. We used JMA files for 1998-2024 and the Smithsonian GVP eruption list (snapshot 2026-11-09) for 89 Holocene volcanoes and 61 confirmed onsets with a known day at 16 volcanoes. The planned alarm was on when the previous 30 days had at least 5 events at 10 km depth or less within 10 km, and at least 3 times the count expected from the year before. The alarm was on before 6 of 61 onsets (9.8%, 95% volcano-bootstrap interval 2.9-21.1%). It was on for 3.9% of days at the same volcanoes, which gives a probability gain of 2.5 (0.8-5.1). Only 11 of 1,407 alarm episodes at the 89 volcanoes (0.8%) were followed by an onset within 30 days. Four of the six hits had alarms only 1-6 days before onset. A threshold-free rank score gave 0.59 (0.49-0.71), where 0.5 is no skill. Low-frequency events gave no skill (1 of 61 hits). Eight sensitivity rules gave point gains of 2.0-3.7, and three had intervals above 1 without correction for multiple tests. For 22 onsets, mostly at island volcanoes, the catalog had no nearby event before onset, so a precursor cannot be seen there. Main limitations: the unified catalog does not contain all volcano-network earthquakes, the sample is small, and onset dates can be uncertain. Code, plan, aggregate results, figures and input hashes are included. Raw JMA and GVP data and GVP-derived record tables are not included and are regenerated by scripts.

display.caption: Observed count of shallow JMA events within 10 km in the 30 days before each of 61 Japanese eruption onsets (1999-2024), against the count expected from the prior year. Orange points are onsets with the alarm on. The dashed line is the alarm limit. Most onsets are near or below the no-change line, and 22 onsets had no events and an expected count below 1.

Hit rate (orange, with 95% volcano-bootstrap interval) and alarm-time fraction at the erupted volcanoes (blue) for the primary rule and sensitivity rules. G is the probability gain and P is the fraction of alarm episodes followed by an onset.

Fraction of the 61 onsets with the alarm on, against days from onset, for shallow events (left) and low-frequency events (right). The dashed line is the alarm-time fraction of all valid days at the same volcanoes.
